scope: Six existing I/O groups, both profiles, unchanged historical Java timing baseline. No all-70-group, all-overload, or end-to-end consumer performance acceptance.
protocol: Two warmups and five measured calls, three independent sequential processes per phase, Node 24.22.2 with --expose-gc. Controls preceded experiments and candidates. First use is in an initialized process; heap samples are neither peak nor retained memory.
limits: The initial exploration omitted --expose-gc and is excluded from protocol comparison.
Structural projection caching did not reliably improve the target and was reverted. Its original measurements are retained.
Individual N-Quads process ratios remain above 1.10 even though both profile process medians meet it. Variance remains visible; no robust all-process pass is claimed.
Performance reports precede formatting-only edits to the writer. Their original source hashes are preserved; structural replay covers the formatted source.

The independent structural sink proves the exact declaration fixtures, identity, annotations/imports and cross-reader results; API metadata, malformed inputs, and other structural families retain separate functional tests.

nativeSemantics.scope: Six 100-class declaration I/O groups only; not full API, metadata, malformed-input or byte-for-byte serializer parity. Untimed sinks do not replace historical Java timings.
nativeSemantics.relativePathReplay: The same 34 observations also passed from two external working directories: relative downloaded JAR paths and relative Java-home path resolve to the same admitted absolute paths.
